info.title: Map dual raw+signal value pattern (@explore subagent)

parts.text:
In /Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view, enumerate every class that holds BOTH a raw/static value field AND a `Signal<T>` field for the SAME logical property (e.g. `private final String value; private final Signal<String> valueSignal;`), with `of(...)` factory overloads for each.

Check these files and report the exact pattern for each: Text.java, Label.java, Image.java, Audio.java, Video.java, Slider.java, Toggle.java, TextField.java, TextEditor.java, DatePicker.java, ColorPicker.java, Stepper.java, Picker.java, Menu.java, Background.java, ForegroundStyle.java, AccessibilityLabel.java, FontSize.java, FontWeightMod.java, FontDesignMod.java, and any others you find (search all of com/pathland/view).

For each class report:
1. The raw field name + type and the signal field name + type.
2. The exact `public static ... of(...)` overloads (raw, signal, no-arg).
3. In `render(...)`, how the raw value vs signal value is written to the PathlandNode (properties vs propertyBindings).
4. Whether the class is a primitive/leaf View (renders a node), a composite View (body()), or a ViewModifier (sets a property).

Also check: `lib/java/pathland-demo-views` and `lib/java/pathland-view/src/test` for ALL call sites of the raw-value overloads of these classes (e.g. `Text.of("...")`, `Slider.of(0f, ...)` vs `Slider.of(signal, ...)`, `Background.of(Color...)`, `Toggle.of(..., true, on, ...)`, etc.) — quote each call site with file:line.

Be exhaustive and precise. Quote exact code.
Let me start by exploring the directory structure and finding all the relevant files.

9: /**
10:  * A view wrapped by one or more property modifiers (innermost-first) or a custom
11:  * {@link ViewModifier}. Property modifiers apply to the innermost built node and are
12:  * overwritten by outer modifiers (SwiftUI "outermost wins"); reactive modifiers record
13:  * a node-level binding so a signal change re-emits only that property.
14:  */
15: final class Modified implements View {
16: 
17:     /** One property application: a static value or a reactive signal. */
18:     record Prop(int property, Object value, Signal<?> signal) {
19: 
20:         static Prop value(int property, Object value) {
21:             return new Prop(property, value, null);
22:         }
23: 
24:         static Prop reactive(int property, Signal<?> signal) {
25:             return new Prop(property, null, signal);
26:         }
27:     }
28: 
29:     private final View inner;
30:     private final List<Prop> props;
31:     private final ViewModifier modifier;
32: 
33:     private Modified(View inner, List<Prop> props, ViewModifier modifier) {
34:         this.inner = inner;
35:         this.props = props;
36:         this.modifier = modifier;
37:     }
38: 
39:     /** A static property mod. */
40:     static Prop prop(int property, Object value) {
41:         return Prop.value(property, value);
42:     }
43: 
44:     /** A reactive property mod. */
45:     static Prop prop(int property, Signal<?> signal) {
46:         return Prop.reactive(property, signal);
47:     }
48: 
49:     /** Build a property-modifier view from inner + props. */
50:     static Modified props(View inner, Prop... props) {
51:         return new Modified(inner, List.of(props), null);
52:     }
53: 
54:     /** A custom-view-modifier wrapper. */
55:     static Modified modifier(View inner, ViewModifier modifier) {
56:         return new Modified(inner, List.of(), modifier);
57:     }
58: 
59:     @Override
60:     public PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
61:         if (modifier != null) {
62:             return modifier.body(inner).render(env);
63:         }
64:         PathlandNode node = inner.render(env);
65:         for (Prop p : props) {
66:             if (p.signal() != null) {
67:                 Object value = ReactiveValues.from(p.property(), p.signal());
68:                 node.properties.put(p.property(), value);
69:                 node.propertyBindings.put(p.property(), p.signal());
70:             } else {

72:             }

11:     // field is initialized before SplitNavDemo's `.environment(ROUTER, router)` scope
12:     // is pushed, so it resolves on .get() inside body(), at render time.

17:     private static final Color ACTIVE_FG = Color.rgb(0x1A, 0x3A, 0x8C);
18: 
19:     @Override
20:     public View body() {
21:         // The router signal resolves here, inside SplitNavDemo's pushed
22:         // .environment(Navigation.ROUTER, router) scope.
23:         return VStack.of(Alignment.FILL, 8,
24:                         Text.of("Pathland").modifiers(
25:                                 FontSize.of(18), FontWeightMod.of(FontWeight.BOLD)),
26:                         menuRow("/home", "Home", "/_pathland/assets/icons/home.svg"),
27:                         menuRow("/kitchen", "Kitchen sink", "/_pathland/assets/icons/kitchen.svg"),
28:                         menuRow("/settings", "Settings", "/_pathland/assets/icons/settings.svg"),
29:                         Spacer.of()
30:                 ).modifiers(Padding.of(16))
31:                 // Fixed-width sidebar with no height hint: as a flex child of the split
32:                 // HStack it stretches to the row's full height (align-items: stretch).
33:                 // Alignment is omitted so the stack's own FILL child-alignment (stretch
34:                 // the menu rows) is preserved.
35:                 .modifier(FrameMod.of(200f))
36:                 .modifier(Background.of(SIDEBAR_BG))
37:                 .modifier(Border.of(SIDEBAR_BORDER, 1f))
38:                 // The sidebar is the app's primary navigation region → a `<nav>` landmark.
39:                 .modifier(AccessibilityRole.of(Roles.NAVIGATION))

257:     /**
258:      * A test sink that keeps every completed frame (the built-in {@link FrameOpcodeSink}
259:      * keeps only the last one — a reactive node with several bindings emits one delta
260:      * frame per binding).
261:      */
262:     private static final class AccumulatingSink implements OpcodeSink {
263: 
264:         private final List<Frame> frames = new ArrayList<>();
265:         private final List<Opcode> ops = new ArrayList<>();
266:         private final ByteArrayOutputStream strings = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
267: 
268:         List<Frame> frames() {
269:             return frames;
270:         }
271: 
272:         @Override
273:         public void beginFrame() {
274:             ops.clear();
275:             strings.reset();
276:         }
277: 
278:         @Override
279:         public void endFrame() {
280:             frames.add(new Frame(List.copyOf(ops), strings.toByteArray()));
281:         }
282: 
283:         private void push(int category, int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
284:             ops.add(new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c));
285:         }
286: 
287:         private void writeString(String text) {
288:             byte[] utf8 = text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
289:             strings.write(utf8.length & 0xFF);
290:             strings.write((utf8.length >>> 8) & 0xFF);
291:             strings.write((utf8.length >>> 16) & 0xFF);
292:             strings.write((utf8.length >>> 24) & 0xFF);
293:             strings.writeBytes(utf8);
294:         }
295: 
296:         @Override
297:         public void createNode(int id, int component) {
298:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0);
299:         }
300: 
301:         @Override
302:         public void deleteNode(int id) {
303:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0);
304:         }
305: 
306:         @Override
307:         public void insertChild(int parent, int child, int index) {
308:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index);
309:         }
310: 
311:         @Override
312:         public void removeChild(int parent, int child) {
313:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0);
314:         }
315: 
316:         @Override
317:         public void moveChild(int parent, int child, int newIndex) {
318:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex);
319:         }
320: 
321:         @Override
322:         public void setText(int nodeId, String text) {
323:             int offset = strings.size();
324:             writeString(text);
325:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, offset, 0);
326:         }
327: 
328:         @Override
329:         public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
330:             int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
331:             if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
332:                 int offset = strings.size();
333:                 writeString((String) value);
334:                 push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
335:             } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN) {
336:                 int offset = strings.size();
337:                 writeString(((Color) value).token());
338:                 push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
339:             } else {
340:                 push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b,
341:                         ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
342:             }
343:         }
344: 
345:         @Override
346:         public void setDate(int nodeId, int days, int millisOfDay) {
347:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
348:         }
349: 
350:         @Override
351:         public void setDesignToken(String path, int valueType, Object value) {
352:             int pathOffset = strings.size();
353:             writeString(path);
354:             int c;
355:             if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
356:                 c = strings.size();
357:                 writeString((String) value);
358:             } else {
359:                 c = ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value);
360:             }
361:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, 0, pathOffset, valueType, c);
362:         }

# Key takeaways

1. The **8 classes with true dual raw+signal fields for the same property**: `Text`, `Label`, `Image`, `Toggle` (leaf/composite Views) and `Background`, `ForegroundStyle`, `AccessibilityLabel`, `FontSize` (ViewModifiers) — plus the internal `Modified.Prop` record that backs all four modifiers.
2. **`render()` writes raw vs signal differently per class**: leaf Views use `node.text`/`node.textBinding` (Text, TextField, TextEditor) or `node.properties.put(...)` + `node.propertyBindings.put(...)` (Image, Audio, Video, Slider, Toggle's SELECTED, Stepper, Picker, ColorPicker) or `node.days`/`node.dateBinding` (DatePicker). ViewModifiers never render a node — they produce a `Modified.props(content, Modified.prop(property, valueOrSignal))`; `Modified.render` (lines 65–72) resolves the signal into `properties.put` + `propertyBindings.put`.
3. **`Toggle` is the only class that writes BOTH a raw `properties.put(SELECTED, ...)` and a `propertyBindings.put(SELECTED, ...)` for the same property** — the raw `selected` is the initial value and the signal takes over reactively.
4. **`Slider` has no raw-value overload** — the user's `Slider.of(0f, ...)` example does not exist; the only signature is `Slider.of(WritableSignal<Float>, float min, float max)`.
5. **`FontWeightMod` and `FontDesignMod` do not participate in the dual-field pattern** — raw-only, no signal overload.
6. `Audio`/`Video`/`TextEditor`/`ColorPicker` are **signal-only** (with a no-arg `of()` for Audio/Video but no raw source overload), and `TextField`/`DatePicker`/`Picker`/`Stepper`/`Menu` mix a raw field for a **different** configuration property with a signal for the value/selection.
